rules.rule: Run `karni context` before reading any files. It prints the current apps, models, viewsets, UI components, hooks, pages and installed modules in a few hundred tokens. Trust it.
rules.rationale: The inventory is derived live from the app registry, the router and the @karni/ui manifest, so it is never stale and costs far fewer tokens than crawling source.

rules.rule: Run `karni rules` at the start of a session and follow what it returns; the adapter files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, ...) only point here.
rules.rationale: One source of truth exposed through the CLI cannot drift between tools.

rules.summary: Model changed: make migrate && karni types.
rules.rule: After any model change run `make migrate && karni types`.
rules.rationale: Migrations and the frontend's TS types + typed hooks are derived from the models; skipping either leaves the API and the UI out of sync.

rules.summary: karni rules --check FILE; karni check before commit.
rules.rule: Run `karni rules --check <file>` on files you write and `karni check` before committing — every enforced rule fails the build, nothing only warns.
rules.rationale: Enforced rules fail CI anyway; catching them while editing is cheaper.

rules.rule: Opt-outs are inline and REQUIRE a reason: Python `# karni: allow(<rule-id>): <why>`; ESLint `// eslint-disable-next-line karni/<rule> -- <why>`; jscpd `// jscpd:ignore-start -- <why>`.
rules.rationale: Rules without escape hatches cause forks, and a fork is worse than a duplicate — but every exception must say why so it can be reviewed.
rules.fix: Write the reason after the marker.

rules.rule: Prefer the standard procedures for routine work: new-model, new-page, add-module, new-module — `karni rules --procedure <name>`, or the matching slash command where your tool has one.
rules.rationale: The procedures encode the shortest correct path for routine work.

rules.rule: Use the project commands (`karni --help` lists them all): `make up` starts the stack; `make migrate` runs makemigrations + migrate; `karni types` regenerates TS types + typed hooks from the API schema; `karni check` runs architecture and system checks; `karni context` prints the inventory; `karni make <type>` scaffolds; runners like `karni test`, `karni shell`, `karni routes`, `karni worker`, `karni schedule list` wrap manage.py/celery/pytest.
rules.rationale: They run inside the right interpreter (project .venv or compose service).

rules.summary: Before editing a file: karni context --with-history FILE.
rules.rule: This project keeps a prompt-history store. Before editing a file that already has history, run `karni context --with-history <file>` and read its HISTORY section, so you do not redo a decision that was already made and reverted.
rules.rationale: The inventory shows what the code contains now; the history provider shows what was already asked, decided and abandoned for that file.

rules.summary: Scaffold via karni make, not by hand.
rules.rule: Create apps, models, viewsets, serializers, migrations, tasks, schedules, events, listeners, management commands, services, middleware, pages, components and modules with `karni make <type>` (`karni make --list`; `--dry-run` previews, `--help` per type). Never hand-create a file, class or route a generator makes — run it, then edit what it wrote.
rules.rationale: Generators emit the conventions in one step (BaseModel, a mandatory access declaration, settings and route markers, ruff-clean imports) and are tested to pass every rule; hand-written scaffolding drifts.
rules.fix: Delete the hand-written scaffold and run the matching `karni make` command.

rules.rule: Karni already implements everything generic; you write only domain code. Extending Karni is always cheaper than reinventing it.
rules.rationale: Generic code written per project is the boilerplate Karni exists to remove.

rules.summary: Never write auth, users, admin, serializers, routers, settings, infra, tables, forms.
rules.rule: Never write auth flows, user models, admin registration, serializers, routers, settings, Docker/Compose config, Celery config, HTML tables, forms, or detail views. Karni provides all of these. If you think you need one, you need an override on an existing Karni base instead.
rules.rationale: Each of these ships in Karni with tested defaults and override points.
rules.fix: Find the Karni base that provides it (`karni context` BASES) and override it.

rules.rule: If an existing component or base class almost fits, extend it through its override props / hooks (`columns`, `fields`, `slots`, `AdminMeta`, `APIMeta`, overridable methods). Do not create a parallel variant.
rules.rationale: A forked variant stops receiving fixes and doubles the surface to maintain.

rules.rule: The stack is fixed. Do not introduce a state library, form library, table library, HTTP client or CSS framework beyond what Karni ships (TanStack Query/Table, react-hook-form, Zod, Tailwind, Radix via @karni/ui). Backend HTTP clients are allowed only in services modules (K105).
rules.rationale: Every extra library is a second way to do something Karni already does.

rules.rule: Backend code per entity goes in `<app>/models.py` and `<app>/viewsets.py` — nothing else. No admin.py, serializers.py, forms.py; urls.py only for non-API endpoints such as webhooks (viewsets ride the auto-router).
rules.rationale: Admin, serializers, filters, routes and schema are derived from those two.

rules.rule: Frontend pages live in `frontend/src/pages/`, one file per page, with the route registered alongside the existing pages.
rules.rationale: The page cap (K202) and the inventory (`karni context` PAGES) rely on it.

rules.rule: Anything reusable across projects belongs in a Karni module (a `karni_<name>` package), not in this project — say so instead of building it.
rules.rationale: Code that would be written more than once belongs in Karni, never per project.

rules.rule: Configure an installed module only through the settings it documents; never patch its internals.
rules.rationale: Patched internals break on the module's next release.

rules.summary: Models inherit BaseModel or compose its mixins.
rules.rule: Models inherit `karni.models.BaseModel` (= `UUIDModel` + `TimestampedModel` + `SoftDeleteModel` + `AuditedModel`), or compose those mixins directly when a model should not have all four (e.g. an append-only log: `UUIDModel, TimestampedModel`). Declare `APIMeta` / `AdminMeta` only for fields that must be hidden, read-only or write-only.
rules.rationale: The mixins supply uuid ids, timestamps, soft delete, audit stamping and the managers the derived API/admin rely on.

rules.rule: Viewsets inherit `karni.api.BaseViewSet` — usually just `model = X` plus its `access` declaration (K109) (+ `search_fields`); the auto-router registers it.
rules.rationale: BaseViewSet derives serializer, filters, pagination, permissions and schema.

rules.rule: Do not register a plain `ModelAdmin`. Declare `AdminMeta` on the model (the admin is derived), or subclass `karni.admin.KarniModelAdmin`.
rules.rationale: The derived admin stays consistent with the model and the API.
rules.fix: Delete the admin class and use AdminMeta, or subclass KarniModelAdmin.

rules.rule: No raw SQL (`.raw()`, `cursor.execute()`, `RawSQL`) outside `*/sql/*` or migrations.
rules.rationale: Raw SQL bypasses managers (soft delete, owner scoping) and the ORM's safety.
rules.fix: Use the ORM, or move the query into a `sql/` module.

rules.rule: Import `requests` / `httpx` / `urllib.request` only in `*/services/*` or `*/providers/*` modules.
rules.rationale: External calls in one layer are mockable, retryable and auditable.
rules.fix: Move the call into a services module and call that.

rules.rule: Never write a Meta-only `ModelSerializer`; `BaseViewSet(model=X)` generates it.
rules.rationale: A redundant serializer silently diverges from the generated one.
rules.fix: Delete it; customise via APIMeta or override get_serializer_class().

rules.rule: No structurally duplicated code (8+ identical statements in two places); reuse the named Karni API or extract one implementation.
rules.rationale: Duplicates are where boilerplate creeps back in.
rules.fix: Call the existing implementation instead of copying it.

rules.rule: `AuditedModel` stamps `created_by`/`updated_by` from the current request. Outside a request (Celery tasks, management commands) nothing is stamped unless you wrap the writes in `with current_user(user):` from `karni.middleware`. Never assign `created_by`/`updated_by` by hand.
rules.rationale: One stamping path keeps the audit trail trustworthy under WSGI, ASGI and workers.
rules.fix: from karni.middleware import current_user; with current_user(user): ...

rules.rule: Every `BaseViewSet` declares `access = Access(read=..., write=...)` (`create=` defaults to `write`), built from `Owned("<fk to user>")`, `HasRole(...)`, `Authenticated()`, `Public()` and `Where(lambda request: Q(...))` combined with `|` / `&`. Reads are public only when you write `Public()`. A viewset without `access` denies every request; `Unscoped(reason=...)` is the explicit opt-out.
rules.rationale: One declaration compiles into both the request gate and the row filter, so neither can be forgotten; a forgotten permission class fails open silently.

rules.rule: Express who sees which rows in `access` (`Where(...)` for custom logic, `@action(..., access=...)` for one action). An overridden `get_queryset` is still read-scoped — never use it to widen. Overriding `filter_queryset_for_user` needs `# karni: allow(access-override): <why>`.
rules.rationale: The queryset is the authoritative layer: lists, details, actions, relation PKs and ?expand= all go through the read scope, so a bypass leaks everywhere.
rules.fix: Move the condition into access (Where(lambda request: Q(...))), or add the marker.

rules.rule: Lists stay bounded and flat. A list-returning `@action` returns `self.paginated_response(queryset)`, never `Serializer(qs, many=True).data`; `pagination_class = None` needs `pagination = Unpaginated(max_rows=N, reason=...)`. Query counts must not grow with rows: BaseViewSet derives select_related/prefetch_related from the serializer, so hint only what it cannot see (SerializerMethodField, properties) with `select_related = [...]` / `prefetch_related = [...]` on the viewset. Raise a budget only with `query_budget = Budget(list=N, reason=...)`.
rules.rationale: An unpaginated list or an N+1 passes with test data and falls over with real data; the scaling check (2 vs 12 rows) and per-action query budgets catch both in CI.
rules.fix: Return self.paginated_response(qs); hint opaque fields with prefetch_related.

rules.rule: Screens compose `@karni/ui` components (`Page`, `ResourceTable`, `ResourceForm`, `ResourceDetail`, ...). Never hand-roll a table or form: no raw `<table>/<form>/<input>/<select>/<textarea>`.
rules.rationale: The components already handle data, validation, a11y and theming.
rules.fix: Compose ResourceTable / ResourceForm / Input / Select from @karni/ui.

rules.rule: Page files stay at 50 lines or fewer. Past that you are rebuilding something Karni ships — use the component's props.
rules.rationale: A long page is reimplementing a component.
rules.fix: Use the components' props; move logic into hooks.

rules.rule: Import only the public `@karni/ui` barrel, never `@karni/ui/dist/*` or `/src/*`.
rules.rationale: Internals change without notice; the barrel is the versioned API.

rules.summary: Data only via Karni hooks; no fetch/axios.
rules.rule: Data access only via @karni/ui hooks (`useResourceList`, `useResourceItem`, `useResourceMutations`, the KarniClient) and the typed hooks generated by `karni types`. No fetch/axios/XMLHttpRequest/WebSocket outside `src/api/`.
rules.rationale: The hooks share caching, auth, errors and query-key invalidation.
rules.fix: Use the generated typed hook or useKarniClient().

rules.rule: No duplicated frontend code above the `frontend/.jscpd.json` threshold.
rules.rationale: Duplicates are where boilerplate creeps back in.
rules.fix: Extract one component or hook, or compose the existing @karni/ui one.

procedures.name: new-model
procedures.description: Add a domain model the Karni way (model + viewset, nothing else)
steps: Run `karni context` to see existing apps, models and viewsets.

`karni make model <Name> <field:type ...> --with viewset --access <who> [--search f1,f2] [--app <app>]` writes the model on `karni.models.BaseModel` and its viewset (`-a` also adds list/detail/form pages). Field types: `karni make model --help`. `--access`: authenticated (default), public-read, owned:<fk to user>, staff, role:<name>; edit the generated `access` for anything richer (`Owned(...) | HasRole(...)`, `Where(...)`). Do NOT write an admin, serializer or router: the auto-router registers it; admin, filters, schema are derived.
Add `class APIMeta:` / `class AdminMeta:` only for fields that must be hidden, read-only or write-only.
`karni make migration && karni migrate && karni types`
Verify: `karni context` lists the model and viewset; GET /api/<plural>/ works for a caller `access` admits and is refused (401/403) or empty for one it does not.
procedures.outro: Total new code should be well under 20 lines. If it isn't, stop — you are reimplementing something Karni provides.

procedures.name: new-page
procedures.description: Add a frontend page composing @karni/ui (50 lines or fewer)
steps: Run `karni context` for available components, hooks, resources and pages.

`karni make page <name> --resource <resource> --kind list|detail|form` writes `frontend/src/pages/<name>.tsx` composing @karni/ui and does the rest a person would do by hand: register the route alongside the existing pages (frontend/src/routes.tsx). Without `--resource` it is a bare `<Page>`. Never hand-roll tables, forms or fetching.
Custom behaviour goes through props (`columns`, `fields`, `rowActions`, slots, custom cell/field renderers) — extend, never fork a variant.
Keep the file at 50 lines or fewer. Data access only via @karni/ui hooks (`useResourceList`, `useResourceItem`, `useResourceMutations`) and the typed hooks generated by `karni types`.
`karni rules --check <the page file>` must report no violations.

procedures.name: add-module
procedures.description: Install an optional Karni module and wire it into settings
steps: Run `karni add <module>` — it adds the `karni-<module>` dependency to pyproject.toml, wires `karni_<module>` into the INSTALLED_APPS block marked `# karni:apps` in config/settings.py, and (once installed) records the module's agent guidance.
Rebuild/install: `docker compose build` (or `uv pip install -r pyproject.toml` in a host venv), then `make migrate`; run `karni add <module>` again if it asked you to.
Run `karni context` — the module must appear under MODULES; `karni rules` now includes its guidance.
Configure only settings the module documents; do not patch its internals.
To create a new reusable module instead: `karni make module <name>` (modules/karni-<name>/, docs/modules.md).

procedures.name: new-module
procedures.description: Create a new local Django app following Karni conventions
steps: Run `karni context` first — confirm the domain isn't already covered.

`karni make app <app_name>` writes `__init__.py`, `apps.py`, `models.py`, `viewsets.py`, `migrations/`, `tests/` and adds the app to the `# karni:apps` block in config/settings.py. No admin.py, serializers.py, urls.py, forms.py — Karni derives all of that.
Add models with `karni make model <Name> <field:type ...> --app <app_name> --with viewset --access <who>` (procedure new-model).
`karni make migration && karni migrate && karni types`, then `karni context` to verify.
Anything reusable across projects belongs in a Karni module: `karni make module <name>`, not in this project — say so instead of building it.
